{{Short description|American basketball player (born 2001)}} {{use mdy dates|date=March 2025}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Richie Saunders | image = Richie Saunders.jpg | alt = | caption = Saunders in 2024 | number = 15 | team = BYU Cougars | position = [[Shooting guard]] | conference = [[Big 12 Conference]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2001|9|19}} | birth_place = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 5 | weight_lb = 200 | high_school = [[Wasatch Academy]]
([[Mount Pleasant, Utah]]) | college = [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] (2022–2026) | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2026) * First-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2025) * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Most Improved Player (2025) }} '''Richie Saunders''' (born September 19, 2001) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]] of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. ==Early life and high school== A great-grandson of [[Ore-Ida]] founder and inventor of the [[Tater Tot]] F. Nephi Grigg,{{Cite news |last=Reynolds |first=Kevin |date=2025-03-20 |title=A BYU basketball player became the face of Tater Tots in March Madness. Here’s why. |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/byu-cougars/2025/03/20/byus-richie-saunders-is-new-face/ |access-date=2025-03-20 |work=The Salt Lake Tribune |language=en-US}} Saunders attended [[Wasatch Academy]]. Coming out of high school, Saunders was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was the 3rd ranked prospect from Utah in the class of 2020. He committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]] over offers from [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]], [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]].{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |last2=Ireland |first2=Kyle |title=Wasatch Academy’s Richie Saunders Commits To BYU Basketball |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu/richie-saunders-byu-basketball-commits-wasatch-academy/420559 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2022–23, Saunders appeared in 34 games with two starts, averaging 5.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Drew |first1=Jay |title=Richie Saunders is the Renaissance man on BYU’s nationally ranked basketball team |url=https://www.deseret.com/2024/1/24/24046898/byu-cougars-richie-saunders-is-renaissance-man-on-mark-pope-nationally-ranked-basketball-team/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} In 2023–24, he appeared in 34 games with one start and averaged 9.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Weber |first1=Alex |title=BYU guard Richie Saunders enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.on3.com/transfer-portal/news/byu-guard-richie-saunders-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/ |website=On3.com |access-date=13 March 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=BYU’s Richie Saunders Announces He Will Enter NCAA Transfer Portal |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu/richie-saunders-byu-basketball-ncaa-transfer-portal/515077 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} Saunders entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]] after the season, but ultimately chose to return to play for BYU.{{cite web |last1=Payne |first1=Jackson |title=Why Richie Saunders should be a First Team All-Big 12 selection |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2025/03/03/byu-basketball-richie-saunders-all-big-12-consideration/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} Heading into his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year, he become a full-time starter for the first time in his career.{{cite web |last1=Payne |first1=Jackson |title=BYU’s Egor Demin, Richie Saunders both set to return from injury for the start of Big 12 play |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/12/30/egor-demin-richie-saunders-returning-from-injury-byu-basketball/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} On December 31, 2024, Saunders posted a career-high 30 points in a victory over [[2024–25 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]].{{cite web |last1=Harmon |first1=Dick |title=Veteran Saunders wrecks ASU with career high in BYU’s Big 12 opener |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/12/31/richie-saunders-byu-cougars-arizona-state-basketball-big-12-opener/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} On January 11, 2025, he tallied 26 points in a loss to [[2024–25 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]].{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=Kevin Young On BYU’s Richie Saunders: ‘As Talented As Any Wing In The Country’ |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu-basketball/richie-saunders-wing-byu-basketball-kevin-young-talented-country-big-12/535686 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} On February 22, Saunders scored 25 points including the pair of game-winning free throws versus [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]].{{cite web |last1=McCann |first1=Dave |title=The ‘S’ in Saunders is for Superman |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2025/02/24/byu-guard-richie-saunders-playing-role-of-super-hero/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} For his performance during the 2024–25 season, he was named the Big 12 Most Improved Player while also being named first-team all-Big 12.{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=BYU’s Richie Saunders, Egor Demin Earn Big 12 Basketball Awards |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu-basketball/richie-saunders-award/541446 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=12 March 2025}} == References ==
